title: Learning Mixture Models via Efficient High-dimensional Sparse Fourier Transforms
text: Unfortunately, the analysis of [ PS15-SFT ] has error that relies on the L 2 L_{2} norm of g g which is not suitable for statistics applications. For this reason we have to analyze the algorithm of [ PS15-SFT ] in a different way to make sure that our error only depends on the modulus of g g on the queried points. We give more details about this in Section 2.1 . Once we have recovered x ⋆ ​ ( t ⋅ v 1 ) , … , x ⋆ ​ ( t ⋅ v m ) x^{\star}(t\cdot v_{1}),\dots,x^{\star}(t\cdot v_{m}) we have the m × k m\times k inner products between d d -dimensional vectors { ⟨ μ j , v ℓ ⟩ } j ∈ [ k ] , ℓ ∈ [ m ] \{\langle\mu_{j},v_{\ell}\rangle\}_{j\in[k],\ell\in[m]} and we can extract the true means μ 1 , … , μ k ∈ d \mu_{1},...,\mu_{k}\in{}^{d} by solving a linear system. The remaining part is to determine how to pick the projections v 1 , … , v m v_{1},...,v_{m} . For this we use the idea of [ kalai2010efficiently ] for learning mixture models, where they project along directions that are sufficiently close to each other. The benefit of projecting along close-by directions is that the ordering of the means can be preserved with high probability.
